1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Reparent a tree on a selected node.
4: 
5: A [tree][wiki-tree] is a special type of [graph][wiki-graph] where all nodes are connected but there are no cycles.
6: That means, there is exactly one path to get from one node to another for any pair of nodes.
7: 
8: This exercise is all about re-orientating a tree to see things from a different point of view.
9: For example family trees are usually presented from the ancestor's perspective:
10: 
11: ```text
12:     +------0------+
13:     |      |      |
14:   +-1-+  +-2-+  +-3-+
15:   |   |  |   |  |   |
16:   4   5  6   7  8   9
17: ```
18: 
19: But there is no inherent direction in a tree.
20: The same information can be presented from the perspective of any other node in the tree, by pulling it up to the root and dragging its relationships along with it.
21: So the same tree from 6's perspective would look like:
22: 
23: ```text
24:         6
25:         |
26:   +-----2-----+
27:   |           |
28:   7     +-----0-----+
29:         |           |
30:       +-1-+       +-3-+
31:       |   |       |   |
32:       4   5       8   9
33: ```
34: 
35: This lets us more simply describe the paths between two nodes.
36: So for example the path from 6-9 (which in the first tree goes up to the root and then down to a different leaf node) can be seen to follow the path 6-2-0-3-9.
37: 
38: This exercise involves taking an input tree and re-orientating it from the point of view of one of the nodes.
39: 
40: [wiki-graph]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_(graph_theory)
41: [wiki-tree]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_(discrete_mathematics)

That's the bug! When the child's reorientation returns a tree, the child has already consumed the parent link — the parent shouldn't keep that child as a child, because the child is now the root. In my implementation, I'm appending the reoriented child to the parent's children, but that's wrong when the child is the new root.

The standard approach: when the target is found in a subtree, the reoriented subtree becomes the new root, and the old parent becomes its child. So the recursion should return the reoriented tree only when it's the new root, and otherwise return the modified subtree.

Better approach: use a sentinel. If the child is the new root, return it as the root (don't append to the parent). Let me restructure:

    children = []

            return result  # propagate up
        children.append(result)

```

Use a sentinel object. Actually, more simply: since the reoriented tree's label is always from_node, we can check `result.label == from_node`. But the sentinel is cleaner. Let's use a module-level sentinel.

Actually, the simplest is: check `if result.label == from_node: return result`. Since the new root's label is exactly from_node. This works and is clean.
